l: Hell, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: Hell is the place from which Ahura Mazda promises to keep the soul away if the prescribed words are pronounced at the last ending of life.

l: soul, Yasna, Yasna LXXI (Sp. LXX).
s: The soul is protected from Hell through the pronunciation of the prescribed words at the last ending of life. It is to pass over the Kinvat Bridge in holiness and come into Heaven.

l: Yasna, Yasna, YASNA LXXII. (See Y. LXI.)
s: The unit is titled YASNA LXXII and refers the reader to YASNA LXI. No further subject, event, or teaching is provided.

l: YASNA LXXII, Yasna, YASNA LXXII. (See Y. LXI.)
s: YASNA LXXII is identified as a unit and directs the reader to see YASNA LXI.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: Visparad I announces and completes Yasna offerings to the lords of spiritual, earthly, aquatic, terrestrial, winged, wild, and cloven-hoofed creatures. It concerns the Yearly festivals, the Gâthas, the Yasna Haptanghâiti, ritual chants, seasons, mountains, deities, and other holy lords of the ritual order. It also includes offerings to settlements of the future, praises and Myazdas, questions and lore of Ahura, and a farm-house with pastures for blessed cattle.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: Visparad I contains announcements and completions of Yasna offerings to various holy lords, festivals, chants, beings, places, and ritual observances.

l: Yasna, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Yasna is announced and completed for the lords of many kinds of creatures, the Yearly festivals, the Seasons, the Gâthas, ritual chants, Ahura's questions and lore, and other holy subjects. It is also celebrated and completed for praises, Myazdas, the Yasna Haptanghâiti, and named divine beings.

l: ritual Order, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The holy lords of the ritual order include lords of spiritual, earthly, aquatic, terrestrial, winged, wild, and cloven-hoofed creatures. They also include the Yearly festivals, named Gâthas, ritual chants, and other beings and places addressed in the announcements and Yasna offerings.

l: Yearly festivals, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Yearly festivals are addressed as lords of the ritual order. They include Maidhyô-zaremaya, Maidhyô-shema, Paitishahya, Ayâthrima, Maidhyâirya, and Hamaspathmaêdhaya.

l: Gâtha Ahunavaiti, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Gâtha Ahunavaiti is announced and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. It is mentioned together with women who bring forth many sons of many talents and with a chant that has its Ahû and Ratu before it in the Yasna.

l: Yasna Haptanghâiti, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Yasna Haptanghâiti is celebrated and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. The text also associates it with the water Ardvi Anâhita.

l: Gâtha Ustavaiti, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Gâtha Ustavaiti is announced and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. It is addressed together with mountains that shine with holiness and are abundantly brilliant and Mazda-made.

l: Gâtha Spentâ-mainyu, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Gâtha Spentâ-mainyu is announced and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. It is mentioned together with Verethraghna, described as the blow of victory and Ahura-given.

l: Gâtha Vohu-khshathra, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Gâtha Vohu-khshathra is announced and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. It is addressed together with Mithra of the wide pastures and Râman Hvâstra.

l: Gâtha Vahistôisti, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: The Gâtha Vahistôisti is celebrated and completed as holy and ruling in the ritual order. It is mentioned after the offerings to the Gâtha Vohu-khshathra, Mithra, and Râman Hvâstra.

l: Ahura, Visparad, Visparad / Visparad I.
s: Ahura is associated with questions asked of Ahura and with the lore of Ahura. The text also names the Ahurian Dahvyuma and the Ahurian Zarathustrôtema as holy lords of the ritual order.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The speaker uses the Zaothra and Baresman to approach and praise spiritual, earthly, aquatic, terrestrial, animal, seasonal, ritual, and other chieftains. The unit concerns Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, Asha Vahista, the holy Yearly festivals, the Gâthas, several named divine beings, settlements, and ritual authorities. It presents praise and homage as directed toward those who uphold the ritual order, righteousness, creation, fertility, victory, blessing, and the advancement of settlements.

l: Zaothra, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The speaker performs this Zaothra while approaching and praising numerous lords, festivals, Gâthas, divine beings, people, and places.

l: Baresman, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The speaker uses this Baresman together with the Zaothra when approaching and praising the entities named in the unit.

l: ritual Order, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The lords of the ritual are approached with praise and are associated with spiritual and earthly authority, the water and land, animals, festivals, seasons, chants, Gâthas, and other ritual powers.

l: holy Yearly festivals, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The holy Yearly festivals are approached with praise as lords of the ritual order, including Maidhyô-zaremaya, Maidhyô-shema, Paitishahya, Ayâthrima, Maidhyâirya, and Hamaspathmaêdhaya.

l: settlements, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The future one of the settlements is approached with praise, and settlements are said to be advanced in the righteous order by the actions of the man who maintains the Mãthra of the Saoshyant.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Ahura Mazda is approached with praise as the spiritual lord and regulator of the spiritual creation. He is said to have mentioned the chieftains of the ritual to Zarathustra for sacrifice and homage because of Asha Vahista, and to reveal lore in answer to a question.

l: Righteous Order, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Asha Vahista is approached when lauded and is identified as the reason the chieftains of the ritual were mentioned for sacrifice and homage.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Zarathustra Spitâma is approached with praise as the terrestrial lord and regulator of the terrestrial creation.

l: Gâtha Ahunavaiti, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Gâtha Ahunavaiti is approached with praise. A chant associated with it is described as having the Alva and the Ratu.

l: Yasna Haptanghâiti, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The heroic Yasna Haptanghâiti is approached in praise as holy and ruling in the ritual order.

l: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is approached in praise as holy and ruling in the ritual order.

l: Gâtha Ustavaiti, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Gâtha Ustavaiti is approached with praise as holy and ruling in the ritual order.

l: Gâtha Spentâ-mainyu, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Gâtha Spentâ-mainyu is approached with praise alongside the holy mountains and Verethraghna.

l: Verethraghna, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Verethraghna is approached with praise as the Mazda-given blow of victory and the holy lord of the ritual order. It is associated with Victorious Ascendency.

l: Gâtha Vohu-khshathra, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Gâtha Vohu-khshathra is approached with praise as holy and ruling in the ritual order.

l: Mithra, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: Mithra of the wide pastures is approached with praise together with the Gâtha Vohu-khshathra, Râman Hvâstra, and other sacred entities.

l: Gâtha Vahistôisti, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Gâtha Vahistôisti is approached with praise together with Mithra of the wide pastures, Râman Hvâstra, and other sacred entities.

l: Airyemâ-ishyô, Visparad, Visparad II.
s: The Airyemâ-ishyô is approached with praise together with the Fshûshô-mãthra and the Hadhaokhdha, which are identified as holy lords of the ritual order.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: Visparad III. begins the Haoma Offering with the Zaotar’s roll-call of priests and other members of the community. The Zaotar calls for the Hâvanan, Âtarevakhsha, Frabaretar, Âberet, Âsnatar, Raêthwiskar, and Sraoshâvareza, while the Ratu answers that he will come or fulfil their duties. The Zaotar also summons priests, warriors, tillers, householders, rulers, youths, women, holy men, chiefs of the Mazdayasnians, the Bounteous Immortals, and the Saoshyants. At the close, the Zaotar and Ratu identify their ritual roles, and the Zaotar declares that he will recite the Staota Yêsnya with memorised intoning, chanting, and praise.

l: Visparad III., Visparad, Visparad III.
s: Visparad III. begins the Haoma Offering and presents the roll-call of the priest.

l: Haoma Offering, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Haoma Offering begins with the Zaotar’s summons and the roll-call of the priest.

l: Zaotar, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Zaotar calls for priests, community members, chiefs of the Mazdayasnians, the Bounteous Immortals, and the Saoshyants. He identifies himself as the Zaotar and declares that he will recite the Staota Yêsnya with memorised intoning, chanting, and praise.

l: Ratu, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Ratu answers the Zaotar’s calls and says that he will come or fulfil the duties and services assigned to the named priests. The Ratu is also described as holy and learned, and as speaking from righteousness.

l: youth of holy thoughts, words and works, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The youth of holy thoughts, words and works is summoned. This youth is described as having a good conscience, good speech, and being given in marriage to his kin.

l: Ahura, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: Ahura is addressed when the Zaotar summons His wives and describes a woman as being like the bounteous Âramaiti.

l: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The chiefs of the Mazdayasnians are summoned, along with the Fire-priests, warriors, and diligent husbandmen of the Mazdayasnian Faith.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Bounteous Immortals are summoned by the Zaotar.

l: Saoshyants, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The pious Saoshyants are summoned as prophets for help. They are described as correct and truthful in speech, zealous, glorious in thought, great, and powerful.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Mazdayasnian Faith is associated with its Fire-priests, warriors, and diligent husbandmen, who are summoned.

l: Staota Yêsnya, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: The Zaotar declares that he will recite the Staota Yêsnya with memorised intoning, chanting, and praise.

l: holy thoughts, words and works, Visparad, Visparad III.
s: Holy thoughts, words and works are associated with the summoned youth, woman, and holy man. The woman is advanced in them, and the holy man is advanced in his good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: The unit concerns sacrifice to thoughts of the mind, good wisdom, good and blessed sanctity, good religious knowledge, and good health of soul and body. It states that confession is to be made for the Kine. Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate at the sacrificial time for the Myazda-offering and at the time for the Ratufrîti. These acts include prayer for blessings, sacrificial worship, homage, propitiation, and praise of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean).

l: confession, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: Confession is to be made for the Kine.

l: Kine, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: The Kine is the recipient for whom confession is to be made.

l: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate at the sacrificial time for the Myazda-offering and at the time for the Ratufrîti.

l: Myazda-offering, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: The Myazda-offering has a sacrificial time at which Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate.

l: Ratufrîti, Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: The Ratufrîti is a time at which Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate, and it is associated with the prayer for blessings.

l: praise of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean), Visparad, Visparad IV (Sp. V).
s: Praise of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean) is included among the acts performed at the sacrificial time.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The speaker comes to the Bountiful Immortals as a praiser priest, invoker, memoriser, reciter, and chanter for their sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. The speaker also prepares for the Saoshyants, their prayer for blessings and sanctification, and the victorious smiting of foes, which is beneficial and holy for their souls. The speaker offers the Bountiful Immortals the flesh of his body and all the blessings of his life, and confesses belief in Ahura Mazda as a Mazdayasnian of the order of Zarathustra and in accordance with his Faith.

l: speaker (the praiser priest), Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The speaker comes as a praiser priest, invoker, memoriser, reciter, and chanter for the Bountiful Immortals’ sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. The speaker offers the Bountiful Immortals the flesh of his body and all the blessings of his life, and confesses his belief in Ahura Mazda.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are addressed as the recipients of the speaker’s sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, offering, and preparation. They are described as ruling and disposing of all aright.

l: Saoshyants, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The Saoshyants are addressed in connection with preparation, well-timed prayer for blessings, sanctification, and the victorious smiting of foes. Their work is described as beneficial for souls and holy.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: Ahura Mazda is addressed by the speaker, who confesses belief in Him.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: Zarathustra is identified as the one whose order the speaker follows as a Mazdayasnian.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The speaker identifies himself as a Mazdayasnian of the order of Zarathustra and says that his belief is in accordance with the Faith.

l: belief in Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad V (Sp. VI).
s: The speaker confesses his belief in Ahura Mazda as part of being a Mazdayasnian of the order of Zarathustra and in accordance with the Faith.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad VI (Sp. VII).
s: Visparad VI (Sp. VII) calls the good Amesha Spenta by their names of beauty and worships the Bountiful Immortals by their beautiful names. It does so in accordance with the precept, with praise, and with the joyful reception of grace. It includes intelligently offered Zaothras and correctly spoken sacrificial words. The ritual Order and Righteousness the good are invoked through blessing.

l: Visparad VI (Sp. VII), Visparad, Visparad VI (Sp. VII).
s: Visparad VI (Sp. VII) calls the good Amesha Spenta by their names of beauty and worships the Bountiful Immortals by their beautiful names. It acts with praise, the joyful reception of grace, intelligently offered Zaothras, and correctly spoken sacrificial words.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad VI (Sp. VII).
s: The good Amesha Spenta are called by their names of beauty.

l: Righteousness the good, Visparad, Visparad VI (Sp. VII).
s: Righteousness the good provides a longing blessing in the ritual observance.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The unit concerns worship of Sraosha, Ashi, Nairya-sangha, Peace, the Fravashis, the Kinvat Bridge, and the Garô Nmâna of Ahura, identified with Heaven and the Best World. It praises the better path to the Best World, Arstât as Justice and the Mazdayasnian Faith, Rashnu, Mithra, Parendi, Heroism, and Mazda-made Sleep. It venerates ancient institutions predating the sky, water, land, plants, and the Kine, along with the sea Vouru-kasha, Mazda-made stormy wind, and the shining heaven. It also worships Fire as Ahura Mazda's son, the ritual Baresman, and Apãm-napât.

l: Sraosha, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Sraosha, identified as Obedience, is worshipped as blessed.

l: Ashi, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Ashi is worshipped as good and blessed, and as the blest order of the rites.

l: Garô Nmâna of Ahura, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The Garô Nmâna of Ahura is worshipped as Heaven, the best world of the saints, shining and all glorious.

l: Heaven, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Heaven is identified with the Garô Nmâna of Ahura and is described as the best world of the saints, shining and all glorious. The shining heaven is also worshipped as an ancient, first-made earthly object of the earthly world.

l: Best World, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The Best World is described as the destination of a better path that is worshipped.

l: Arstât, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Arstât is worshipped as good Justice, which helps settlements advance and flourish. Arstât is identified with the Mazdayasnian Faith.

l: ancient institutions, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The ancient institutions are worshipped as things in the creation of the holy that were formed before the sky, water, land, plants, and the Kine of blessed gift.

l: sea Vouru-kasha, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The sea Vouru-kasha is worshipped.

l: Mazda, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Mazda is associated with the making of the stormy wind and Sleep. Sleep made by Mazda gladdens the herd and men.

l: Fire, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Fire is worshipped as Ahura Mazda's son and as the holy lord of the ritual order.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: Ahura Mazda is identified as the one whose son is Fire, and whose Garô Nmâna is worshipped as Heaven.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad VII (Sp. VIII).
s: The Mazdayasnian Faith is identified with Arstât, the good Justice that helps settlements advance and flourish.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad VIII (Sp. IX).
s: The unit addresses Ahura Mazda with a proper word and asks that He be present. Ahura Mazda is invoked together with the good Yazads, identified as the Bountiful Immortals who rule and dispose of all aright. The Kingdom is assigned to Him who rules the best.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad VIII (Sp. IX).
s: Ahura Mazda is approached and summoned to be present with the proper word. He is invoked as the holy one together with the good Yazads.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad VIII (Sp. IX).
s: The good Yazads are identified as the Bountiful Immortals. They rule aright and dispose of all aright, and are invoked together with Ahura Mazda.

l: Kingdom, Visparad, Visparad VIII (Sp. IX).
s: The Kingdom is to belong to Him who rules the best.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Visparad IX concerns homage and praise offered to Haomas and Zaothras, their future offerings, and the remedies and virtues accompanying them. It also honors Kisti, Mazda, Zarathustra, Zarathustrôtema, the good Mazdayasnian Faith, Prayer for blessings, and other sacred words and practices. The unit approaches the strength of the strong, Rectitude and Blessedness, Kisti, the Bountiful Immortals, Good Mind, Universal Weal and Immortality, the Kine and Kine's Soul, the Fire of the spoken name, and a sanctified farm-house. It presents sacrifice, homage, and praise as directed toward Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Mãthra Spenta, the Mazdayasnian Religion, the Yasnas, the lords of the ritual, and the entire creation of the holy.

l: Visparad IX (Sp. X), Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Visparad IX concerns homage, praise, sacrifice, and propitiation directed toward sacred beings, virtues, practices, and the entire creation of the holy.

l: Haomas and Zaothras, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Haomas and Zaothras are offered, will yet be offered, and are described as smiting victoriously and being foes of hatred. They accompany healing virtues, Kisti, the remedies of Mazda, those of Zarathustra and the Zarathustrôtema, the good Mazdayasnian Faith, Prayer for blessings, good veracity, and the pious word against unbelief.

l: Kisti, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Kisti is identified with religious knowledge and is associated with the remedies of Mazda, Zarathustra, and the Zarathustrôtema. It is also honored together with the Priority for the powerful Ascendency.

l: Mazda, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The remedies of Mazda accompany certain offered Haomas and Zaothras.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The remedies of Zarathustra accompany certain offered Haomas and Zaothras.

l: Ahurian Zarathustrôtema, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The remedies of the Zarathustrôtema accompany certain offered Haomas and Zaothras.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The good Mazdayasnian Faith is associated with offered Haomas and Zaothras that accompany it.

l: good and pious Prayer for blessings, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The pious and beneficent Prayer for blessings is associated with offered Haomas and Zaothras. A well-timed prayer for blessings is also included in the ritual praise.

l: Rectitude and Blessedness, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Rectitude and Blessedness are described as powerful and are approached with homage and praises.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are powerful Yazads who rule aright and dispose of all aright. They are ever-living and ever-helpful, dwell together with the Good Mind, and are included in sacrifice, homage, and praise.

l: Good Mind, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The Good Mind is the companion with whom the male and female Bountiful Immortals dwell together.

l: Universal Weal and Immortality, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Universal Weal and Immortality are approached for homage and praises.

l: Kine, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The body of the Kine is approached for homage and praises.

l: Kine's Soul, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The Kine's Soul is approached for homage and praises.

l: sacrifice, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Sacrifice is presented as an offering of praise and homage to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the holy and lofty Lord, blessedness, Mãthra Spenta, the Mazdayasnian Religion, the Yasnas, the lords of the ritual, well-timed prayers for blessings, and the entire creation of the holy.

l: homage, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Homage is offered or desired toward Haomas and Zaothras, sacred powers and beings, Universal Weal and Immortality, the Kine and Kine's Soul, and the holy creation.

l: praise of Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The praise of Ahura Mazda is identified as a praise used for sacrifice and homage.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Ahura Mazda is praised in the ritual as part of sacrifice and homage.

l: Mãthra Spenta, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: Mãthra Spenta is identified as the bounteous word of reason and is included in the praise used for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and glorification.

l: Yasna, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The Yasnas are included among the praises used for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and glorification.

l: entire creation of the holy, Visparad, Visparad IX (Sp. X).
s: The entire creation of the holy is the object of sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and glorification.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad X (Sp. XI).
s: The speaker desires to approach several entities with praise. These include the Arezahis, Savahis, Fradadhafshu, Vîdadhafshu, Vouru-baresti, Vouru-garesti, and the Karshvar which is Hvaniratha. The speaker also praises ritual objects, the Ahuna-vairya, ritual prayers beside Ahuna, and the standing offices of the Mazdayasnian Faith.

l: Karshvar which is Hvaniratha, Visparad, Visparad X (Sp. XI).
s: The Karshvar which is Hvaniratha is among the entities the speaker desires to approach with praise.

l: Baresman, Visparad, Visparad X (Sp. XI).
s: The Baresman is spread with sanctity, and the speaker desires to approach it with praise.

l: Ahuna-vairya, Visparad, Visparad X (Sp. XI).
s: The Ahuna-vairya is among the entities the speaker desires to approach with praise.

l: standing offices of the Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad X (Sp. XI).
s: The standing offices of the Mazdayasnian Faith are among the things the speaker desires to approach with praise.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The unit concerns offerings, celebrations, and ritual announcements made to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, divine beings, Fravashis, and the entire creation of the holy and clean. Haomas, ritual implements, waters, prayers, recitations, and other sacred objects are presented for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, victory, sanctification, and the well-being of souls. The celebrations are also intended to benefit and protect the house, its herds and retainers, and the saints connected with it. The Avesta is declared according to the directions of Ahura Mazda and Zarathustra, and the speakers identify themselves as holy Saoshyants.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Ahura Mazda receives presented Haomas, offerings, celebrations, and sacred objects. His Fire is invoked, and the Avesta is said to be directed by him.

l: Haomas, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Haomas and Haoma-implements are presented to Ahura Mazda, Verethraghna, the Bountiful Immortals, the good waters, the souls, and the entire creation of the holy. Haoma-water, holy Haoma, and Haoma mixed with milk and Hadhânaêpata are included in the offerings.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The Bountiful Immortals receive Haomas, celebrations, offerings, sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. They are described as ruling and disposing aright, ever-living, ever-helpful, good, bestowers of the good, and dwelling with the Good Mind.

l: good and pious Prayer for blessings, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The prayer for blessings is uttered at the fitting and well-timed moment and is presented in the celebration. It is associated with the order of the prayers, victory, sanctification, and the well-being of souls.

l: Fire of Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The Fire of Ahura Mazda receives announcement and presentation in the celebration. Its perfume and its role in sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise are included among the sacred offerings.

l: Sraosha, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Sraosha, identified as Obedience the blessed, receives announcement and presentation in the celebrations. He is included among those for whom sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise are performed.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The Fravashis of the saints receive announcement, sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. They include the Fravashis of the dead, the living, the unborn, and the prophets who shall serve and bring the renovation of the completed world.

l: sacrifice, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Sacrifice is performed for Ahura Mazda, divine beings, Fravashis, and the entire creation of the holy and clean. The offerings and celebrations are made for sacrifice together with homage, propitiation, and praise.

l: homage, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Homage is offered in the celebrations to Ahura Mazda, divine beings, Fravashis, and the entire creation of the holy and clean. The Avesta and ritual prescripts are declared for this purpose.

l: propitiation, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Propitiation is included among the purposes of the offerings and celebrations. It is directed toward Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Fravashis, and the entire creation of the holy and clean.

l: Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma receives announcement in the celebration for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: Zarathustra Spitâma is identified as holy and is said to have directed how the Avesta should be said. His Fravashi is honored in the celebrations.

l: house, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The celebrations are made promotive and beneficial for the house, for the furtherance and increase of its household. They are intended to overcome restrictions and harmful malice, and to bless its herds and retainers, born and yet to be born.

l: Saoshyants, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The speakers say that they belong to the house as the Saoshyants of the provinces. They identify themselves as holy Saoshyants and associate their preparation with the success of prayer, victory, sanctification, and the well-being of souls.

l: saints, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The saints receive offerings, announcements, and honors through their Fravashis and souls. The unit refers to saints of the house, saints who do good deeds, and saints whose deeds are conspicuously good.

l: Avesta, Visparad, Visparad XI (Sp. XII).
s: The Avesta is made known as an offering and is said to be what holy Ahura Mazda directed to be said and what Zarathustra directed. The priest declares that he understands its lawful and legitimate form and its ritual prescripts.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The unit concerns offerings of Haomas to Ahura Mazda and Zarathustra Spitama, seeking abundance in cattle and men and the aid of Sraosha. It offers the Ahuna-vairya, the two mortars, correctly spoken words, Zarathustrian utterances, ceremonies, Baresmans, pressed Haomas, praises, Yasnas, and the doctrines of the Mazdayasnian Religion. These ritual deeds, precepts, and teachings are connected with Ahura Mazda, Vohu Manah, the Righteous Order, and Spenta Mainyu's world. The two mortars are asked to become full of wisest meaning for the Mazdayasnians and their communities.

l: Haomas, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Haomas are offered in libation to Ahura Mazda and Zarathustra Spitama. They are pressed correctly and are associated with abundance in cattle and men.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Ahura Mazda receives offerings and is described as the holy One who delivered the ritual deeds and teachings.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Zarathustra Spitama receives libations of the offered Haomas together with Ahura Mazda.

l: Sraosha, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Sraosha accompanies the abundance produced by the offerings with great splendour of sanctity. He is asked to be present with energetic effort to aid worship.

l: Ahuna-vairya, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Ahuna-vairya is offered as a wise offering, both when intoned with sanctity and when yet to be intoned. It possesses many teachings of religious wisdom.

l: religious wisdom, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Religious wisdom is contained in the Ahuna-vairya, correctly spoken words, Zarathustrian utterances, ceremonies, and other ritual practices. Its teachings are imparted and pondered.

l: two mortars, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The two mortars pour out the Haomas and are pushed forward with precision. They are asked to become full of wisest meaning as they are turned and advanced.

l: Mazdayasnian Faith, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Mazdayasnian Religion is represented through its praises, Yasnas, doctrines, recitations, and movements.

l: ritual deeds, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Ritual deeds are offered in the creation and imparted with their many points of meaning. Ahura Mazda delivered them, and they have nourishment from Vohu Manah and growth from the Righteous Order.

l: precepts, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The precepts are described as containing the wisest meaning and incitations. They are imparted to the chosen within Spenta Mainyu's world.

l: Vohu Manah, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Vohu Manah is described as providing nourishment for the ritual deeds.

l: Righteous Order, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Righteous Order is described as providing growth for the ritual deeds.

l: Spenta Mainyu's world, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: Spenta Mainyu's world is where the speakers seek to be while imparting precepts and incitations of the wisest meaning.

l: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians, Visparad, Visparad XII (Sp. XIV).
s: The Mazdayasnians are steadfast in worship and appear with wood-billets, perfumes, and supplicated blessings. The mortars are asked to become full of wisest teaching for them.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: Visparad XIII (Sp. XV) describes ritual worship and sacrifice. It names Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Zarathustra, the Mãthra, the blessings for the saints, and the hail addressed to the Bountiful Immortals. It also honors the three principal chapters, their Hâs, metrical lines, words, word-structure, recital, memorising, chanting, and steadfast offering, without addition or omission.

l: Visparad XIII (Sp. XV), Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: Visparad XIII (Sp. XV) sets out ritual worship and sacrifice to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the sacrificial word correctly spoken, every Mãthra, Zarathustra, the blessings for the saints, and the hail addressed to the Bountiful Immortals. It also honors the three principal chapters and their parts without addition or omission.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped according to the ritual.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped according to the ritual. The hail addressed to them is also worshipped.

l: ritual, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: The ritual prescribes worship of Ahura Mazda and the Bountiful Immortals, as well as sacrifice to sacred words, Zarathustra, the blessings for the saints, and the hail addressed to the Bountiful Immortals.

l: Mãthra, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: Every Mãthra is treated as a sacred word of reason and is included among the objects of sacrifice. Zarathustra is identified as especially the possessor of the Mãthra.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: Zarathustra is sacrificed to as especially the possessor of the Mãthra.

l: three principal chapters, Visparad, Visparad XIII (Sp. XV).
s: The three principal chapters are uttered and worshipped without addition or omission. Their entirety, Hâs, metrical lines, words, word-structure, recital, memorising, chanting, and steadfast offering are also honored.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI). concerns worship and sacrifice directed to Ahura Mazda, the Gâtha Ahunavaiti, and the Ahuna-vairya. It describes the Gâtha Ahunavaiti through its measures, word-structure, Zand, questions and counter-questions, words, metric feet, recitation, worship, wisdom, clearness, loving intention, sovereignty, ritual order, and acquired boon. It also identifies the Ahuna-vairya as the holy lord of the ritual order and describes offerings to the constituent parts of the Gâtha Ahunavaiti.

l: Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI)., Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI). presents worship and sacrifice to Ahura Mazda, the Gâtha Ahunavaiti, and the Ahuna-vairya. It also describes the constituent parts and qualities associated with the Gâtha Ahunavaiti.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the holy Lord of the ritual order. He is also identified as the one with the titles Ahû and Ratu, and as the giver of the acquired boon for the promotion of piety.

l: Gâtha Ahunavaiti, Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: The Gâtha Ahunavaiti is worshipped and sacrificed to with its measures, word-structure, Zand, questions and counter-questions, words, and metric feet. It is described as well-recited and being recited, well-worshipped and being used in worship, and as having its own wisdom, clearness, loving intention, sovereignty, ritual order, and acquired boon. Its chapters, metrical lines, words, word-structure, heard-recital, memorised recital, continuous offering, and steadfast offering are also worshipped.

l: Ahuna-vairya, Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: The Ahuna-vairya is worshipped as the holy lord of the ritual order. It is described as having its Ahû and its Ratu.

l: ritual Order, Visparad, Visparad XIV (Sp. XVI).
s: The ritual order is associated with Ahura Mazda, who is worshipped as its holy Lord. It is also associated with the Gâtha Ahunavaiti, which is described as having its own ritual order, and with the Ahuna-vairya, which is called its holy lord.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Visparad XV instructs Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians to prepare themselves for lawful deeds in accordance with the sacred Order and to avoid unlawful and evil deeds contrary to the ritual. It directs them to perform good deeds that further husbandry and to render the needy rich. Sraosha is called to be present for the worship and service of Ahura Mazda and for devotion to the Yasna Haptanghâiti. The Yasna Haptanghâiti is to be memorised and recited victoriously, without addition or omission, for the pronunciation of victorious words for Ahura Mazda's Fire.

l: Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII), Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Visparad XV instructs Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians to prepare themselves for lawful deeds, avoid unlawful and evil deeds, further husbandry, and render the needy rich. It calls for Sraosha to be present for the worship of Ahura Mazda and the service, memorisation, and recital of the Yasna Haptanghâiti.

l: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians are told to hold their feet, hands, and understandings in readiness for the well-doing of lawful deeds and the avoidance of unlawful and evil deeds. They are directed to further husbandry through good deeds and to render the needy rich.

l: sacred Order, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: The sacred Order is the standard in accordance with which Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians are to perform lawful deeds.

l: good deeds, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Lawful deeds are to be done in accordance with the sacred Order. Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians are instructed to perform them for well-doing.

l: Sraosha, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Sraosha is called to be present for the worship of Ahura Mazda, for service, and for the pondering, devotion, memorisation, and victorious holy recital of the Yasna Haptanghâiti.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the most helpful and holy. The Yasna Haptanghâiti is used in service to him, and victorious words are pronounced for his Fire.

l: Yasna Haptanghâiti, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: The Yasna Haptanghâiti is to be pondered, devotedly attended to, memorised, and recited victoriously and holily. Its recital is to be without addition or omission and is described as powerful, victory-smiting, and separate from harmful malice.

l: Fire, Visparad, Visparad XV (Sp. XVIII).
s: The Yasna Haptanghâiti is recited for the pronunciation of victorious words for Ahura Mazda's Fire.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: The unit concerns worship of Fire, Ahura Mazda's son, along with Yazads and Rashnus having the seed of fire. It honors Sraosha, the holy man, the entire holy creation, the Blessedness and Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma, and the saints and their Fravashis. It also worships the Fravashis of holy men and women within and outside the Province. It sacrifices to fields, waters, lands, plants, and the parts of the Yasna Haptanghâiti.

l: Fire, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: Fire is worshipped as Ahura Mazda's son. The unit also mentions Yazads and Rashnus as having the seed of fire in them.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: Ahura Mazda is identified as holy. His Yasna has known the service of certain beings as better, with Zarathustra as the living chief and master.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: Fravashis of saints, Zarathustra Spitâma, holy men, and holy women are worshipped. The unit includes Fravashis within and outside the Province and worships them collectively and individually.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: Zarathustra Spitâma is identified as a saint. His Blessedness and Fravashi are worshipped, and he is the living chief and master among those whose service Ahura Mazda has known as better.

l: saints, Visparad, Visparad XVI (Sp. XIX).
s: The saints and their blessed Fravashis are worshipped. The unit also worships the entire creation of the holy and the Fravashis of saints within and outside the Province.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XVII (Sp. XX).
s: Visparad XVII (Sp. XX) concerns striving after the good thoughts, words, and deeds inculcated in the Yasna Haptanghâiti. It states that a blessing is the Right (called) the Best. It says there is weal, including weal for the man who is toward Righteousness Best and right.

l: Visparad XVII (Sp. XX), Visparad, Visparad XVII (Sp. XX).
s: It is the unit in which striving after the good thoughts, words, and deeds of the Yasna Haptanghâiti is stated, along with a blessing concerning the Right (called) the Best and weal.

l: Yasna Haptanghâiti, Visparad, Visparad XVII (Sp. XX).
s: It inculcates good thoughts, words, and deeds, after which they strive.

l: Righteous Order, Visparad, Visparad XVII (Sp. XX).
s: It is described as a blessing, and weal is associated with it.

l: weal, Visparad, Visparad XVII (Sp. XX).
s: It is said to exist, including for the man who is toward Righteousness Best and right.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: The unit concerns worship of Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spenta, the holy man, and the prior world of the holy and the clean. It presents the state of weal and salvation for the holy man as an object of worship. It also describes the life-long state of blessedness for the holy as the evil man's calamity, along with eternal salvation and the salvation prayer. The text calls for sacrifice to every saint who exists, is now coming into existence, or shall exist in future.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped with the usta.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: The Amesha Spenta are worshipped with the usta.

l: holy man, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: The holy man is worshipped with the usta, and the state of weal and salvation for the holy man is worshipped.

l: state of weal and salvation, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: The state of weal and salvation for the holy man is worshipped.

l: life-long state of blessedness, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: The life-long state of blessedness for the holy is worshipped. It is the evil man's calamity.

l: eternal salvation, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: Eternal salvation is worshipped.

l: worship of Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: Worship is offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spenta, the holy man, the prior world of the holy and the clean, states of salvation and blessedness, and eternal salvation.

l: saints, Visparad, Visparad XVIII (Sp. XXI).
s: Every saint who exists, who is now coming into existence, and who shall exist in future receives sacrifice.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII) worships Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Âramaiti, and other holy beings and principles. It offers sacrifice to the bountiful saint, anticipative understanding, Âramaiti, holy creatures, shining sun, glorious achievements, glory, herds with Fire and its blessings, holy benefit, and wisdom. The unit connects Âramaiti with bountiful creatures and with the laws of the Righteous Order. It also describes the sun as highest of the high and worships it together with the Bountiful Immortals and the Mãthras with their good ceremonies.

l: Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII), Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII) worships and sacrifices to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Âramaiti, holy creatures, the sun, and other bountiful or holy realities.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as bountiful and as Him who is Ahura Mazda Himself.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are worshipped with the saying the Spenta. They are also worshipped together with the shining sun.

l: Âramaiti, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: Âramaiti is described as good and bountiful, and as the ready mind. She is worshipped together with the bountiful creatures in the creation of the pure, and her wisdom is associated with the laws of the Righteous Order.

l: holy creatures, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: The holy creatures are sacrificed to and worshipped. They are described as having intelligence or Righteousness as their first quality, and as being associated with Âramaiti and the Righteous Order.

l: sun, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: The sun is described as shining and as the highest of the high. It is worshipped together with the Bountiful Immortals and the Mãthras with their good ceremonies.

l: Righteous Order, Visparad, Visparad XIX (Sp. XXII).
s: The Righteous Order is named in connection with the laws that belong to Âramaiti and the holy creatures who have Righteousness as their first quality.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII) concerns sacrifice and worship offered to the Gâtha Vohu-khshathra, the Vohu-khshathra, and the Khshathra-vairya. It praises the iron-founding and correctly spoken sacrificial words that smite the foe with victory and hold the Daêvas subject. It describes rewards, health, healing, progress, growth, and victorious smiting acquired through the memorised recital of the good thoughts, good words, and good deeds. It also sacrifices to the later Yasna, the heroic Haptanghâiti, which becomes the holy ritual chief as it recurs.

l: Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII), Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII) presents sacrifices and worship offered to the Vohu-khshathra, the Khshathra-vairya, and the later Yasna, the heroic Haptanghâiti.

l: Vohu-khshathra, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The text offers sacrifice to the Vohu-khshathra and describes rewards, health, healing, progress, growth, and victorious smiting as lying between the Vohu-khshathra and the Vahistôisti.

l: Khshathra-vairya, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The Khshathra-vairya is identified as the kingdom to be desired, and sacrifice is offered to it.

l: Daêvas, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The correctly spoken sacrificial words are said to hold the Daêvas subject.

l: Vahistôisti, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The Vahistôisti is named as the other point between which the listed rewards, health, healing, progress, growth, and victorious smiting are found.

l: memorised recital of the good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The memorised recital of the good thoughts, good words, and good deeds is said to acquire rewards, health, healing, progress, growth, and victorious smiting. It is used for withstanding evil thoughts, words, and deeds and for undoing treacherous thoughts, false words, and unfair deeds.

l: the later Yasna, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The text offers sacrifice to the later Yasna.

l: Yasna Haptanghâiti, Visparad, Visparad XX (Sp. XXIII).
s: The heroic Haptanghâiti is identified with the later Yasna and is described as becoming the holy ritual chief as it recurs.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Visparad XXI concerns earnest Yasna and homage offered to the good waters, fertile fruit-trees, Fravashis of the saints, Kine, Gaya (Maretan), Mãthra Spenta, Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the lofty lord, and the Bountiful Immortals. It also concerns sacrifice to listening, mercy, hearing of homage, and mercy shown in response to praise. The passage further offers sacrifice to the frârâiti vîdushê, the good praise without hypocrisy or malice, the later Yasna and its offering, and the chapters, metrical lines, words, and word-structure of the later Yasna.

l: Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV), Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Visparad XXI concerns earnest Yasna and homage to good beings and sacrifice to forms of listening, mercy, praise, and the later Yasna.

l: Yasna, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: The Yasna is taken up earnestly for the good waters, fertile fruit-trees, Fravashis of the saints, Kine, Gaya (Maretan), Mãthra Spenta, Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the lofty lord, and the Bountiful Immortals. The passage also sacrifices to the later Yasna, its offering, chapters, metrical lines, words, and word-structure.

l: homage, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Homage is offered earnestly to the good waters, fertile fruit-trees, Fravashis of the saints, Kine, Gaya (Maretan), Mãthra Spenta, Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the lofty lord, and the Bountiful Immortals. The passage also sacrifices to the hearing of spoken homage.

l: the good waters, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: The good waters receive earnest Yasna and homage.

l: the fertile fruit-trees, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: The fertile fruit-trees, which bear as of themselves, receive earnest Yasna and homage.

l: Fravashis of the saints, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: The Fravashis of the saints receive earnest Yasna and homage.

l: Mãthra Spenta, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Mãthra Spenta, described as the bounteous word-of-reason and as holy, receives earnest Yasna and homage.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Ahura Mazda receives earnest Yasna and homage.

l: Zarathustra, Visparad, Visparad XXI (Sp. XXIV).
s: Zarathustra receives earnest Yasna and homage.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV) concerns a chant performed for the Bountiful Immortals and the holy Saoshyants. Through the chant and accompanying ceremonial actions, the speakers offer supplications for the Kine. The chant is recognized by the saint as good and fruitful of blessed gifts, but is unknown to the sinner. The speakers pray that the sinner will not outstrip them in thought, words, ceremonies, or offerings when approaching for harm.

l: Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV), Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV) contains a chant and describes its associated ceremonial actions and supplications for the Kine.

l: chant, Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: The chant is fully chanted for the Bountiful Immortals and the holy Saoshyants. The saint recognizes it as good and fruitful of blessed gifts, while the sinner does not know it.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: The Bountiful Immortals are among those for whom the chant is performed.

l: Saoshyants, Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: The holy Saoshyants are described as prophets who shall serve the speakers, and the chant is performed for them.

l: Kine, Visparad, Visparad XXII (Sp. XXV).
s: The Kine are the subject of the speakers' supplications, which they utter through the chant and accompanying ceremonial actions.

l: Visparad, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: The unit concerns worship offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spenta, Asha Vahista, Heaven, and other best things. Asha Vahista is identified as Righteousness the Best, while Heaven is described as the best world of the saints, bright and all-glorious. The text also concerns the best approach leading to Heaven and the reward, health, healing, furtherance, increase, and victory associated with the Ahuna-vairya and Airyemâ-ishyô. These benefits are connected with the memorised recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Ahura Mazda, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as the best.

l: Bountiful Immortals, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: The Amesha Spenta are worshipped as the best.

l: Righteous Order, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: Asha Vahista is worshipped and identified as Righteousness the Best. The best wish is described as being that of Asha Vahista.

l: Heaven, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: Heaven is worshipped as the best world of the saints, bright and all-glorious. The text also refers to the best approach that leads to Heaven.

l: victory, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: Victory is among the rewards, health, healing, furtherance, and increase associated with the Ahuna-vairya and the Airyemâ-ishyô through the memorised recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Ahuna-vairya, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: The Ahuna-vairya is one of the two through which victory and other benefits are found by the memorised recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Airyemâ-ishyô, Visparad, Visparad XXIII (Sp. XXVI).
s: The Airyemâ-ishyô is one of the two through which victory and other benefits are found by the memorised recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Âfrînagân presents ritual services and blessings for Hâvani, the seasonal lords, the Gâthas, and Rapithwina. It instructs Mazdayasnians to offer Myazda or, if unable, equivalent liquor or wood, and prescribes expulsion and penance for those who fail to bring the required offerings. It blesses rulers with strength, victory, long life, health, and Heaven. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin teaches that performing the Rapithwina office with the prescribed ritual preparations earns a reward like the wind that advances and blesses the material world.

l: Âfrînagân, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Âfrînagân contains sections for Gahanbâr, Gâtha, and Rapithvin observances. It prescribes offerings, blessings, disciplinary measures, and ritual procedures.

l: Ahura Mazda, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Mazda is worshipped as Ahura Mazda, the resplendent and glorious Lord. Sovereign Power is ascribed to Ahura Mazda, who rules best, and Mazda grants or declares the rewards and ritual instructions described.

l: Zarathustra, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Zarathustra is named as the founder of the order followed by the speaker and as the one to whom Ahura Mazda speaks. He asks Ahura Mazda what reward is acquired by performing the Rapithwina ritual.

l: Mazdayasnians, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Mazdayasnians are instructed to offer the ritual service and present the appropriate Myazda. Those who fail to bring required Myazda may be expelled from among the Mazda-worshippers.

l: Gâh Hâvan, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Hâvani is the holy lord and regulator of the ritual order for whose sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise the service is performed. Hâvani presides over the ritual at its appointed time.

l: Righteousness the Best, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Ritual Righteousness is described as a lofty lord who receives worship, homage, propitiation, and praise. It is also identified with the best blessing, weal, and right conduct toward it.

l: Maidhyô-zaremya, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Maidhyô-zaremya is named as a lord to whom propitiation, homage, and praise are offered. Its Myazda consists of sound flesh from a choice beast with a full flow of milk, or an equivalent substitute when necessary.

l: Myazda, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Myazda is an offering associated with each of the six seasonal observances. A person who fails to bring the required Myazda can be expelled by the responsible Ratu and subjected to expiating deeds.

l: Ratu, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: The Ratu guides disciples, receives the Myazda belonging to the observance, and expels disciples who fail to bring it. The Ratu may also impose expiating deeds, while wood may be brought to the Ratu's house when the prescribed offering cannot be made.

l: Âfrîn[-Agân] Gâtha, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Âfrîn[-Agân] Gâtha praises Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and the holy Gâthas. It offers propitiation to the Fravashis of the saints and sacrifice to the five named Gâthas.

l: the Bountiful Immortals, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: The Bountiful Immortals receive praise and propitiation in Âfrîn[-Agân] Gâtha and propitiation in Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin. They are described as ruling aright and disposing of all aright.

l: lofty Gâthas, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: The Gâthas are called bountiful and holy and are said to rule in the ritual order. Ahunavaiti, Ustavaiti, Spentâ-mainyu, Vohu-khshathra, and Vahistôisti each receive sacrifice.

l: Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin concerns Rapithwina, its associated ritual lords, and the reward for performing the Rapithwina office. It records Ahura Mazda's answer to Zarathustra about the merit of the properly conducted observance.

l: Gâh Rapithvin, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: Rapithwina is the ritual time and holy lord of the ritual order named in the text. Its blessing and office are recited with washed hands and mortars, spread Baresman, lifted Haoma, flaming fire, loudly intoned Ahuna-vairya, a Haoma-moistened tongue, and a Mãthra-bound body.

l: the Rapithwina office, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: The Rapithwina office is recited and performed with the Rapithwina prayer for blessing and the prescribed ritual preparations. The person who performs it properly receives a reward like the southern wind that advances, increases, blesses, rejoices, and causes the material world to progress.

l: the Rapithwina ritual, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Âfrînagân. / I. Âfrîn[-Agân] Gahanbâr. .. III. Âfrîn[-Agân] Rapithvin.
s: The Rapithwina ritual requires washed hands and mortars, spread Baresman, elevated Haoma, brightly flaming fire, loud recitation of Ahuna-vairya, a Haoma-moistened tongue, and a Mãthra-bound body. Its proper performance earns the reward declared by Ahura Mazda.

l: Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: The Gâhs are five ritual sections, Gâh Hâvan, Gâh Rapithvin, Gâh Uziren, Gâh Aiwisrûthrima, and Gâh Ushahin, devoted to sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise within the ritual order. They invoke Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the sacred fires, divine beings, Fravashis, and other lords associated with different times, virtues, places, and functions. The sections repeatedly affirm Mazda-worship, opposition to the Daêvas, and devotion to the lore of the Lord. They also bless or sacrifice to powers connected with righteousness, waters, fire, prosperity, strength, obedience, justice, and the advancement of settlements.

l: The Gâhs, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: The Gâhs comprise five ritual sections: Gâh Hâvan, Gâh Rapithvin, Gâh Uziren, Gâh Aiwisrûthrima, and Gâh Ushahin. They prescribe sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and blessing for Ahura Mazda and numerous holy lords of the ritual order.

l: Gâh Hâvan, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Gâh Hâvan is the first Gâh and concerns the holy Hâvani, Sâvanghi, Vîsya, Mithra of the wide pastures, Râman Hvâstra, Fire, Apãm-napât, Nairya-sangha, and others. It includes sacrifice to the five Gâthas and to the words and deeds of Zarathustra.

l: Gâh Rapithvin, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Gâh Rapithvin is devoted to Rapithwina, Frâdat-fshu, Zantuma, Asha Vahista, and Ahura Mazda's Fire. It invokes the Gâthas, correctly spoken words, waters, lands, plants, Fravashis, and the assembly held by the Bountiful Immortals.

l: Gâh Uziren, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Gâh Uziren concerns Uzayêirina, Frâdat-vîra, Dahvyuma, Apãm-napât, and the waters created by Mazda. It sacrifices to the ritual officiants, celestial bodies, later lore, the creation by day and night, Fire, and the water which Mazda created.

l: Gâh Aiwisrûthrima, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Gâh Aiwisrûthrima concerns Aiwisrûthrima, Aibigaya, Frâdat-vîspãm-hugyâiti, and Zarathustrôtema. It invokes Fravashis, women who have many sons, prosperity, strength, the victorious Blow, the sacred vows, social leaders, the house-mistress, and exemplary holy men and women.

l: Gâh Ushahin, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Gâh Ushahin concerns Ushahina, Beregya, Nmânya, Sraosha, Rashnu, and Arstât. It sacrifices to Aurora, the dawn, Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Asha Vahista, Khshathra-vairya, and Âramaiti, and blesses Sraosha, Rashnu, and Arstât.

l: Ahura Mazda, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Ahura Mazda is repeatedly propitiated, worshipped, and sacrificed to as the holy lord of the ritual order and the highest object of the ritual. He is identified as the creator of the waters and as the father of Fire, and his Kingdom is said to offer a nurturer to the poor.

l: Zarathustra, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Zarathustra is named as the model and order-giver of the Mazda-worshippers. Sacrifice is offered to him, his Fravashi, all the words he spoke, and the deeds well done or yet to be done.

l: Mithra of the wide pastures, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Mithra of the wide pastures is described as having a thousand ears and a myriad eyes. He receives sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise, especially in connection with Vîsya and Râman Hvâstra.

l: Râman Hvâstra, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: Râman Hvâstra receives sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise alongside Mithra of the wide pastures. He is also invoked for the worship and exaltation of Vîsya.

l: the Bountiful Immortals, Afrinagan, Gahs and Miscellaneous Fragments, The Gâhs. / I. The Gâh Hâvan. .. V. Gâh Ushahin.
s: The Bounteous Immortals are identified as guardians of the saints. Sacrifice is offered to them, and they are said to hold an assembly and reunion when they gather on the heights of Heaven.
